docs.name: wtPosDecay

docs.name: wtPosRelease

docs.description: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

docs.name: wtWarpRelease
docs.description: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

docs.name: wtWarpRate

docs.name: wtWarpDepth

docs.description: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

docs.name: wtWarpSkew

docs.name: wtWarpMode
docs.description: Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator. The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit, spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip

s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").wtWarp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")
  .wtWarpMode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

docs.name: wtPhaseRand
docs.description: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Randomness of the initial phase. Between 0 (not random) and 1 (fully random)

docs.name: source
docs.description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

docs.name: n
docs.description: Selects the given index from the sample map. Numbers too high will wrap around. n can also be used to play midi numbers, but it is recommended to use note instead.

docs.name: note
docs.description: Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of a letter (a-g or A-G) optional accidentals (b or #) optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3 Examples of valid note names: c , bb , Bb , f# , c3 , A4 , Eb2 , c#5 You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

docs.name: accelerate
docs.description: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

docs.name: velocity
docs.description: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

docs.name: gain
docs.description: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

docs.name: postgain
docs.description: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

docs.name: amp
docs.description: Like gain , but linear.

docs.name: attack
docs.description: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

docs.name: fmh
docs.description: Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio. Controls the timbre of the sound. Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural, while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

docs.name: fm
docs.description: Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth. Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

docs.name: fmenv
docs.description: Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

docs.name: fmattack
docs.description: Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

docs.name: fmwave
docs.description: Waveform of the fm modulator

docs.name: fmdecay
docs.description: Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

docs.name: fmsustain
docs.description: Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

docs.name: bank
docs.description: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with s . The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of s .
examples: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

docs.name: chorus
docs.description: mix control for the chorus effect

docs.name: decay
docs.description: Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level. Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

docs.name: sustain
docs.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

docs.name: release
docs.description: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

docs.name: bpf
docs.description: Sets the center frequency of the b and- p ass f ilter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

docs.name: bpq
docs.description: Sets the b and- p ass q -factor (resonance).

docs.name: begin
docs.description: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. 0.25 to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

docs.name: end
docs.description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

docs.name: loop
docs.description: Loops the sample. Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo. To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

docs.name: loopBegin
docs.description: Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end ). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end , and before loopEnd ! Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

docs.name: loopEnd
docs.description: End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end ). Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end , and after loopBegin !

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

docs.name: crush
docs.description: Bit crusher effect.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

docs.name: coarse
docs.description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

docs.name: tremolo
docs.description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

docs.name: tremolosync
docs.description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

docs.name: tremolodepth
docs.description: Depth of amplitude modulation

docs.name: tremoloskew
docs.description: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: between 0 & 1, the shape of the waveform

docs.name: tremolophase
docs.description: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: the offset in cycles of the modulation

docs.name: tremoloshape
docs.description: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

docs.name: drive
docs.description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

docs.name: duckorbit
docs.description: Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect. Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

docs.name: duckdepth
docs.description: The amount of ducking applied to target orbit Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1") . Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3") .

docs.name: duckonset
docs.description: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume. Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects. Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003") . Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3") .
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

docs.name: duckattack
docs.description: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume. Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003") . Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3") .

docs.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

docs.name: channels

docs.name: pwrate

docs.name: pwsweep

docs.name: phaser
docs.description: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

parameters.name: phasersweep

docs.name: phasercenter

docs.name: phaserdepth
docs.description: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

docs.name: channel
docs.description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

docs.name: cut
docs.description: In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

docs.name: lpf

docs.name: lpenv
docs.description: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

docs.name: hpenv

parameters.name: modulation
parameters.description: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

docs.name: bpenv
docs.description: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

parameters.name: modulation
parameters.description: depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and n

docs.name: lpattack
docs.description: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

docs.name: hpattack
docs.description: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

docs.name: bpattack
docs.description: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

docs.name: lpdecay

docs.name: hpdecay

docs.description: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

docs.name: lpsustain
docs.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

parameters.name: sustain
parameters.description: amplitude of the lowpass filter envelope

docs.name: hpsustain
docs.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

docs.name: bpsustain
docs.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

parameters.name: sustain
parameters.description: amplitude of the bandpass filter envelope

docs.name: lprelease
docs.description: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

docs.name: hprelease
docs.description: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

docs.name: bprelease
docs.description: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

docs.name: ftype
docs.description: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

docs.name: fanchor
docs.description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

docs.name: hpf
docs.description: Applies the cutoff frequency of the h igh- p ass f ilter. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

docs.name: vib
docs.description: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

docs.name: noise
docs.description: Adds pink noise to the mix

docs.name: vibmod
docs.description: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set
examples:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

docs.name: hpq
docs.description: Controls the h igh- p ass q -value.

docs.name: lpq
docs.description: Controls the l ow- p ass q -value.

docs.name: djf
docs.description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.description: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

docs.name: delay
docs.description: Sets the level of the delay signal. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter, separated by ':'.

docs.name: delayfeedback
docs.description: Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay. Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

docs.name: delayfeedback
docs.description: Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay. Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

docs.name: delayspeed
docs.description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

parameters.name: delayspeed
parameters.description: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

docs.name: delaysync
docs.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

docs.name: lock
docs.description: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.

docs.name: detune
docs.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

docs.name: unison
docs.description: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

docs.name: spread
docs.description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

docs.name: dry
docs.description: Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

docs.name: freq
docs.description: Set frequency of sound.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

docs.name: pattack
docs.description: Attack time of pitch envelope.

docs.name: pdecay
docs.description: Decay time of pitch envelope.

docs.name: prelease
docs.description: Release time of pitch envelope
examples:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

docs.name: penv
docs.description: Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

docs.name: pcurve
docs.description: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

docs.name: panchor
docs.description: Sets the range anchor of the envelope: anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv] anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

docs.name: leslie
docs.description: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

docs.name: lrate
docs.description: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

docs.name: lsize
docs.description: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

docs.name: label
docs.description: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

docs.name: octave
docs.description: Sets the default octave of a synth.

docs.name: orbit
docs.description: An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

docs.name: pan
docs.description: Sets position in stereo.

parameters.name: pan
parameters.description: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

docs.name: room
docs.description: Sets the level of reverb. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

docs.name: roomlp
docs.description: Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

docs.name: roomdim
docs.description: Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

docs.name: roomfade
docs.description: Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

docs.name: iresponse
docs.description: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: to use as an impulse response

docs.name: irspeed
docs.description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

docs.name: irbegin
docs.description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

docs.name: roomsize
docs.description: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room . When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

docs.name: shape
docs.description: (Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud. Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

docs.name: distort
docs.description: Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud. Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

docs.name: compressor
docs.description: Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release") More info here

docs.name: speed
docs.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

docs.name: stretch
docs.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

docs.name: unit
docs.description: Used in conjunction with speed , accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed .

docs.name: squiz
docs.description: Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as: "A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

parameters.name: squiz
parameters.description: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

docs.name: vowel
docs.description: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

parameters.name: vowel
parameters.description: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

docs.name: density

docs.name: clip

docs.name: duration
docs.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

docs.name: color

docs.name: adsr

docs.description: MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

docs.description: Sets properties in a batch.

parameters.name: mapping

docs.description: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

docs.name: drawLine
docs.description: Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span. Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up. Character legend: "|" cycle separator "-" hold previous value "." silence

docs.name: euclid
docs.description: Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm. Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common divisor of two numbers. They were described in 2004 by Godfried Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist. Euclidean rhythms are really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: the number of steps to fill

docs.description: Like euclid , but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: the number of steps to fill

examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

docs.name: euclidLegato
docs.description: Similar to euclid , but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: the number of steps to fill

docs.name: euclidLegatoRot
docs.description: Similar to euclid , but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: the number of steps to fill

docs.name: euclidish
docs.description: A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as sound("bd").euclid(3,8) , and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the same as sound("bd bd bd") . sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: the number of steps to fill

parameters.name: groove
parameters.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

docs.name: Pattern
docs.description: Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The function that maps a State to an array of Hap .

docs.name: withValue
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of each hap. It has the alias fmap .

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: to to apply to the value

docs.name: fmap
docs.description: see withValue

docs.name: appWhole
docs.description: Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that pattern of functions.

docs.name: appBoth
docs.description: When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps with those in the given pattern of values. A new pattern is returned, with each matching value applied to the corresponding function. In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

docs.name: appLeft
docs.description: As with appBoth , but the whole timespan is not the intersection, but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets, are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left hand or inner pattern).

docs.name: appRight
docs.description: As with appLeft , but whole timespans are instead taken from the pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer pattern.

docs.name: queryArc
docs.description: Query haps inside the given time span.

docs.name: splitQueries
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to happen within a cycle.

docs.name: withQuerySpan
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

docs.name: withQueryTime
docs.description: As with withQuerySpan , but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the query timespan.

docs.name: withHapSpan
docs.description: Similar to withQuerySpan , but the function is applied to the timespans of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where present, whole timespans).

docs.name: withHapTime
docs.description: As with withHapSpan , but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the hap timespans.

docs.name: withHaps
docs.description: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

docs.name: withHap
docs.description: As with withHaps , but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

docs.name: setContext
docs.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

docs.name: withContext
docs.description: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

docs.name: stripContext
docs.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

docs.name: withLoc
docs.description: Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the context of every hap.

docs.name: filterHaps
docs.description: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

parameters.name: hap_test
parameters.description: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

docs.name: filterValues
docs.description: As with filterHaps , but the function is applied to values inside haps.

docs.name: removeUndefineds
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from query results.

docs.name: onsetsOnly
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time as its part timespan.

docs.name: discreteOnly
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole' timespans) removed from query results.

docs.name: defragmentHaps
docs.description: Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole. Only intended for use in tests.

docs.name: firstCycle
docs.description: Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when debugging a pattern.

parameters.name: with_context
parameters.description: set to true, otherwise the context field will be stripped from the resulting haps.

docs.name: firstCycleValues
docs.description: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

docs.name: showFirstCycle
docs.description: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

docs.name: sortHapsByPart
docs.description: Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

docs.name: layer
docs.description: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose , but without the original pattern:

docs.name: superimpose
docs.description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

docs.name: log
docs.description: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

docs.name: logValues
docs.description: A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters) within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

docs.name: into
docs.description: Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern. True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern to be played unchanged.

docs.name: arpWith
docs.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

docs.name: arp
docs.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

docs.name: add
docs.description: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

docs.name: sub
docs.description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
examples:
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.

docs.name: mul
docs.description: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

docs.name: div
docs.description: Divides each number by the given factor.

docs.name: struct
docs.description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
examples:
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)

docs.name: mask
docs.description: Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

docs.name: reset
docs.description: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

docs.name: restart
docs.description: Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern. While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

docs.name: gap
docs.description: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

docs.name: silence
docs.description: Does absolutely nothing..

docs.name: pure
docs.description: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

docs.name: sequenceP
docs.description: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

docs.name: stack
docs.description: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

docs.name: slowcat
docs.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

docs.name: slowcatPrime
docs.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

docs.name: cat
docs.description: The given items are con cat enated, where each one takes one cycle.

docs.name: arrange
docs.description: Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

docs.name: seqPLoop
docs.description: Similarly to arrange , allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Unlike arrange , you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which means that patterns can overlap.

docs.name: sequence
docs.description: See fastcat

docs.name: seq
docs.description: Like cat , but the items are crammed into one cycle.

docs.name: register
docs.description: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

docs.name: round
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

docs.name: floor
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3 , and -4.2 replaced with -5 .

docs.name: ceil
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4 , and -4.2 replaced with -4 .

docs.name: toBipolar
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

docs.name: fromBipolar
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

docs.name: range
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range. Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

docs.name: rangex
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range, following an exponential curve.

docs.name: range2
docs.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

docs.name: ratio
docs.description: Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":". Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

docs.name: compress
docs.description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

docs.name: fastGap
docs.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

docs.name: focus
docs.description: Similar to compress , but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

docs.name: ply
docs.description: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

docs.name: fast
docs.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

docs.name: hurry
docs.description: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

docs.name: slow
docs.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

docs.name: inside
docs.description: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

docs.name: outside
docs.description: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

docs.name: lastOf
docs.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

docs.name: firstOf
docs.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

docs.name: every
docs.description: An alias for firstOf

docs.name: apply
docs.description: Like layer, but with a single function:

docs.name: cpm
docs.description: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

docs.name: early
docs.description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

parameters.name: cycles
parameters.description: number of cycles to nudge left

docs.name: late
docs.description: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

parameters.name: cycles
parameters.description: number of cycles to nudge right

docs.name: zoom
docs.description: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:
examples:
s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)
// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent

docs.name: bite
docs.description: Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to slice , but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

docs.name: linger
docs.description: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

docs.name: segment
docs.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

docs.name: swingBy
docs.description: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x , which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

docs.name: swing
docs.description: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

docs.name: invert
docs.description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

docs.name: when
docs.description: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

docs.name: off
docs.description: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

docs.name: brak
docs.description: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

docs.name: rev
docs.description: Reverse all haps in a pattern

docs.name: pressBy
docs.description: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

docs.name: press
docs.description: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

docs.name: hush
docs.description: Silences a pattern.

docs.name: palindrome
docs.description: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

docs.name: juxBy
docs.description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

docs.name: jux
docs.description: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

docs.name: echoWith
docs.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

docs.name: echo
docs.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

docs.name: stut
docs.description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

docs.name: plyWith
docs.description: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: function to apply, given the pattern

docs.name: plyForEach
docs.description: The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event. This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

docs.name: iter
docs.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

docs.name: iterBack
docs.description: Like iter , but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

docs.name: repeatCycles
docs.description: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

docs.name: chunk
docs.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

docs.name: chunkBack
docs.description: Like chunk , but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

docs.name: fastChunk
docs.description: Like chunk , but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

docs.name: chunkInto
docs.description: Like chunk , but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

docs.name: chunkBackInto
docs.description: Like chunkInto , but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

docs.name: ribbon
docs.description: Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles . If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: start point of loop in cycles

docs.name: tag
docs.description: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).

docs.name: filter
docs.description: Filters haps using the given function

docs.name: filterWhen
docs.description: Filters haps by their begin time

docs.name: within
docs.description: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: end within cycle (0 - 1). Must be > start

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: function to be applied to the sub-pattern

docs.name: pace
docs.description: Experimental Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

docs.name: polymeter
docs.description: Experimental Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
examples:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

docs.name: stepcat
docs.description: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat , but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat .
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

docs.name: stepalt
docs.description: Experimental Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat , but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

docs.name: take
docs.description: Experimental Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

docs.name: drop
docs.description: Experimental Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

docs.name: extend
docs.description: Experimental extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d" , whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d" .
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

docs.name: expand
docs.description: Experimental Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

docs.name: contract
docs.description: Experimental Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand .

docs.name: shrink
docs.description: Experimental Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with : ), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

docs.name: grow
docs.description: Experimental Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with : ), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

docs.name: tour
docs.description: Experimental Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

docs.name: zip
docs.description: Experimental 'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

docs.name: timecat
docs.description: Aliases for stepcat

docs.name: chop
docs.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

docs.name: striate
docs.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

docs.name: loopAt
docs.description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

docs.name: slice
docs.description: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

docs.name: onTriggerTime
docs.description: make something happen on event time uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

docs.name: splice
docs.description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

docs.name: fit
docs.description: Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to loopAt .

docs.name: loopAtCps
docs.description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be given by a global clock and this function will be deprecated/removed.

docs.name: ref
docs.description: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

docs.name: xfade
docs.description: Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1: 0 = (full left, no right) .5 = (both equal) 1 = (no left, full right)

docs.name: beat
docs.description: creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle especially useful for creating rhythms

docs.name: morph
docs.description: Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same number of true values.

docs.name: pick
docs.description: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to inhabit , but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
examples: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

docs.name: pickmod
docs.description: The same as pick , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

docs.name: pickF
docs.description: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: the array of functions from which to pull

docs.name: pickmodF
docs.description: The same as pickF , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: the array of functions from which to pull

docs.name: pickOut
docs.description: Similar to pick , but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

docs.name: pickmodOut
docs.description: The same as pickOut , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

docs.name: pickRestart
docs.description: Similar to pick , but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

docs.name: pickmodRestart
docs.description: The same as pickRestart , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

docs.name: pickReset
docs.description: Similar to pick , but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

docs.name: pickmodReset
docs.description: The same as pickReset , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

docs.name: inhabit
docs.description: Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to pick , but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

docs.name: inhabitmod
docs.description: The same as inhabit , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

docs.name: squeeze
docs.description: Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

docs.name: setcpm
docs.description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

docs.name: allTransforms
docs.description: Applies a function to all the running patterns. Note that the patterns are groups together into a single stack before the function is applied. This is probably what you want, but see each for a version that applies the function to each pattern separately. $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh8") all(fast("<2 3>")) $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh8") all(x => x.pianoroll())

docs.name: each
docs.description: Applies a function to each of the running patterns separately. This is intended for future use with upcoming 'stepwise' features. See all for a version that applies the function to all the patterns stacked together into a single pattern. $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh*8") each(fast("<2 3>"))

docs.name: square

docs.description: Creates a pattern from a binary number.

parameters.name: n

docs.name: binaryN
docs.description: Creates a pattern from a binary number, padded to n bits long.

parameters.name: n

docs.name: shuffle
docs.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

docs.name: scramble
docs.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle , but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

docs.name: rand
docs.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

docs.name: rand2
docs.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

docs.name: brandBy
docs.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

docs.name: brand
docs.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

docs.name: irand
docs.description: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

docs.name: chooseWith
docs.description: Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

docs.name: chooseInWith
docs.description: As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather than the pattern you're using to choose with.

docs.name: choose
docs.description: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements.

docs.name: choose
docs.description: Chooses from the given list of values (or patterns of values), according to the pattern that the method is called on. The pattern should be in the range 0 .. 1.

docs.name: choose2
docs.description: As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be in the range -1 .. 1

docs.name: chooseCycles
docs.description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

docs.name: wchoose
docs.description: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements by giving a probability to each element

docs.name: wchooseCycles
docs.description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle by giving a probability to each element
examples: wchooseCycles(["bd bd bd",5], ["hh hh hh",3], ["sd sd sd",1]).fast(4).s()

// The probability can itself be a pattern
wchooseCycles(["bd(3,8)","<5 0>"], ["hh hh hh",3]).fast(4).s()

docs.name: perlin
docs.description: Generates a continuous pattern of perlin noise , in the range 0..1.

docs.name: berlin
docs.description: Generates a continuous pattern of berlin noise, in the range 0..1.

docs.name: degradeBy
docs.description: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 0% chance of removal 1 = 100% chance of removal

docs.name: degrade
docs.description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .degradeBy(0.5)

docs.name: undegradeBy
docs.description: Inverse of degradeBy : Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 100% chance of removal 1 = 0% chance of removal Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

docs.name: undegrade
docs.description: Inverse of degrade : Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .undegradeBy(0.5) Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

docs.name: sometimesBy
docs.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability. Similar to someCyclesBy

docs.name: sometimes
docs.description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

docs.name: someCyclesBy
docs.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis. Similar to sometimesBy

docs.name: someCycles
docs.description: Shorthand for .someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)

docs.name: often
docs.description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.75, fn)

docs.name: rarely
docs.description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.25, fn)

docs.name: almostNever
docs.description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.1, fn)

docs.name: almostAlways
docs.description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.9, fn)

docs.name: never
docs.description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0, fn) (never calls fn)

docs.name: always

docs.name: csoundm
docs.description: Sends notes to Csound for rendering with MIDI semantics. The hap value is translated to these Csound pfields: p1 -- Csound instrument either as a number (1-based, can be a fraction), or as a string name. p2 -- time in beats (usually seconds) from start of performance. p3 -- duration in beats (usually seconds). p4 -- MIDI key number (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127]. p5 -- MIDI velocity (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127]. p6 -- Strudel controls, as a string.

docs.name: pianoroll
docs.description: Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll) . To have a pianoroll appear below a pattern instead, prefix with , e.g.: sound("bd sd").pianoroll() .

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

parameters.name: cycles
parameters.description: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

parameters.name: playhead
parameters.description: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

parameters.name: vertical
parameters.description: displays the roll vertically - 0 by default

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

parameters.name: flipTime
parameters.description: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

parameters.name: flipValues
parameters.description: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

parameters.name: overscan
parameters.description: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

parameters.name: hideNegative
parameters.description: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

parameters.name: smear
parameters.description: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

parameters.name: fold
parameters.description: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

parameters.name: inactive
parameters.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent

parameters.name: playheadColor
parameters.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default

parameters.name: fillActive
parameters.description: active notes are filled with color - 0 by default

parameters.name: stroke
parameters.description: notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

parameters.name: strokeActive
parameters.description: active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

parameters.name: hideInactive
parameters.description: only active notes are shown - 0 by default

parameters.name: colorizeInactive
parameters.description: use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default

parameters.name: fontFamily
parameters.description: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

parameters.name: minMidi
parameters.description: minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10

parameters.name: maxMidi
parameters.description: maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90

parameters.name: autorange
parameters.description: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

docs.description: Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels. Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

docs.name: pitchwheel

docs.name: spiral
docs.description: Displays a spiral visual.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

parameters.description: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

parameters.name: cap

parameters.name: steady

parameters.name: activeColor

parameters.name: inactiveColor

docs.name: transpose
docs.description: Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values. The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation. If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with M = major m = minor P = perfect A = augmented d = diminished Examples intervals: 1P = unison 3M = major third 3m = minor third 4P = perfect fourth 4A = augmented fourth 5P = perfect fifth 5d = diminished fifth

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

docs.name: scaleTranspose

parameters.name: offset

docs.name: scale
docs.description: Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale. When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards in the scale as well as sharps or flats (but not both) to produce notes outside of the scale. Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}. A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4 , c , f# , bb4 ) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type . The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

examples: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()

docs.name: rootNotes

docs.name: voicing
docs.description: Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params: chord : Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7 dict : voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary anchor : the note that is used to align the chord mode : how the voicing is aligned to the anchor below : top note <= anchor duck : top note <= anchor, anchor excluded above : bottom note >= anchor offset : whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing n : if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved All of the above controls are optional, except chord . If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.
